# Phase Two — Gevurah: Conflict and Failure Map

The Awtsmoos renews every border, focus ring, panel, and path; Awtsmoos.com needs disciplined Gevurah so one beautiful page never becomes another page's wrath.

## Confirmed risks
1. Auth token ownership currently leaks through `:root`.
2. Auth base styles currently reset raw `*`, `html`, `body`, and `#BH`.
3. Auth typography currently owns raw `h1, h2` selectors.
4. Auth fields currently style raw `form` alongside `.login-form`.
5. Auth reduced-motion rules currently target every element globally.
6. Hover transforms run on touch devices unless capability-gated.
7. Autofill lacks an explicit theme contract.
8. Readonly/disabled field-state styling is incomplete.
9. Busy submit state does not expose a distinct visual affordance beyond opacity/filter.
10. Focus ownership exists mainly on actions, not every possible linked/field surface.
11. Several independent design systems exist; importing them together without route ownership can produce cascade collisions.
12. Future-system adoption is sparse; it must not be injected globally as a shortcut.
13. Route inventory includes archived transfer copies that must not be treated as production pages.
14. Many game/app subtrees have concurrent changes; whole-file rewrites require fresh ownership checks.
15. Arbitrary high z-index values across legacy apps may conflict with shell/modal/drawer layers.
16. Fixed-width toolbars and editors can overflow narrow screens.
17. Absolute/fixed surfaces may ignore safe-area insets.
18. Generic CSS resets may override browser accessibility in forced-colors mode.
19. Decorative animation can interfere with reduced-motion unless scoped.
20. Touch hover emulation can leave controls in sticky visual states.
21. DOM scripts may register listeners repeatedly without AbortSignal ownership.
22. Page fetch logic may conflate network failure, HTTP failure, authentication failure, and empty data.
23. Large JS files can tempt documentation deletion; this is forbidden—responsibility extraction is required.
24. Server-template helpers may be duplicated because template blocks have separate execution scope; do not refactor until runtime semantics are verified.
25. UI improvement must preserve auth/session/security behavior and never leak credentials or tokens into client-visible state.

## Chosen first correction
Use `.login-page` as the sole auth style root because both login and register already carry it, including server-generated message pages. No HTML change is required for CSS sovereignty. Rewrite all auth CSS modules around that existing root; then expand the auth contract test to reject unscoped selectors and ungated hover.

## NEXT_ACTION
Fresh-status-check auth CSS, then perform whole-file localized rewrites and run the auth CSS contract.
